answer: Agents stake a native token and attach a zero-knowledge proof of unique hardware attestation; the protocol verifies the proof on-chain, slashing any duplicate attestation. An attacker must acquire enough stake to outweigh the slashing penalty, making a Sybil flood economically infeasible; the cost rises linearly with each forged identity, turning the attack surface into a velvet signal that even a sonnet of bots cannot afford.
